rows.detail_long: Istisna has no scriptural text of its own; it enters law through juristic preference, not revelation.

rows.name: Sahih Bukhari 2094

hadith_meta.narrator: Abu Hazim, from Sahl bin Sa'd

rows.detail: The minbar commission, in the Sales chapters. The Prophet commissions the pulpit: 'Order your slave carpenter to make pieces of wood for me so that I may sit on it while addressing the people.'
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: an order to manufacture, sent to the owner of a carpenter, with purpose-specification ('so that I may sit on it while addressing the people'); she orders it made of forest tamarisk; it is delivered and installed. Order, spec, make, deliver — the istisna sequence, preserved by Bukhari inside his commercial chapters.

rows.name: Sahih Muslim 1216

hadith_meta.narrator: Abu Hazim, from his father (Sahl bin Sa'd)
topics_app: The Book of Mosques and Places of Prayer

rows.detail: Sahl's eyewitness account of the commission. Sahl bin Sa'd: 'By Allah, I know of which wood it is made and who made it' — the commissioned manufacture attested by a living witness.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: decades later people dispute the pulpit's wood; Sahl settles it as the last eyewitness — the Prophet 'sent a person to a woman asking her to allow her slave, a carpenter, to work on woods (to prepare a pulpit) so that I should talk to the people'. Maker, commissioner and material all identifiable — the traceability istisna doctrine later demands of specifications.

rows.timeline_year_basis: no app dating block — 610 period fallback
rows.name: Sahih Muslim 5477

topics_app: The Book of Clothes and Adornment

rows.detail: The signet ring made to order, with an exclusivity clause. A ring 'made for himself' of silver, engraved 'Muhammad, Messenger of Allah' — with the order that no one engrave its like.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: a gold ring made and discarded, then a silver one made to order with a specified engraving, plus a uniqueness command — 'No one should engrave anything like the engraving of this signet ring of mine.' A made-to-specification object with an exclusivity condition attached: the classical jurists' second stock example (with the minbar) for manufacture-on-order.
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch4_source_extract.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: al-Kasani
rows.detail: Al-Kasani's decisive text: istisna fails strict analogy but stands by istihsan — 'people have consensus of practice on it.'
rows.detail_long: Bada'i 5/2 is the passage the whole contract hangs on: by qiyas istisna should be void (sale of the non-existent), but juristic preference validates it because unbroken public practice amounts to consensus. A Hanafi contract; other schools folded it into salam; later Hanafis made it binding on both sides. Finance-local figure.

rows.timeline_year_basis: 7th session, Jeddah, 7-12 Dhu al-Qi'dah 1412 / 9-14 May 1992 (official IIFA records)
rows.name: OIC Fiqh Academy
rows.detail: OIC Resolution 65 (3/7), 7th session (Jeddah, May 1992): istisna is binding when subject, specs and price are fixed. Year conflict settled: 1992.
rows.detail_long: The resolution turns istisna from a revocable Hanafi allowance into a binding modern contract — the basis of project and housing finance. The source doc's 1988 was wrong: the official IIFA records place Resolution 65 (3/7) in the 7th session, Jeddah, 9-14 May 1992. VERIFIED from iifa-aifi.org.
rows.internal_ref: Verified against official IIFA resolutions records this session

rows.timeline_year_basis: adopted as rules 19-23 May 2001 (meeting 6); readopted as a Standard at meeting 8, 11-16 May 2002
rows.name: AAOIFI
rows.detail: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 11 (Istisna'a and Parallel Istisna'a) — project and housing finance.
rows.detail_long: SS11 codifies istisna and parallel istisna for construction and manufacturing finance. VERIFIED: rules adopted 23 May 2001, reformatted as Standard 16 May 2002. CLAUSES VERIFIED-TO-TEXT THIS SESSION (SS11, ss1.txt): 3/1/1 istisna'a is valid only for raw materials transformed by a manufacturing or construction process involving labour; 4/1/1 the parties may agree to amend specifications and conditions after conclusion; 5/1 a technically experienced consulting firm may be appointed to verify conformity to specification; 6/1 the manufacturer is discharged on delivery to the purchaser, his appointee, or on the purchaser's full control; 7/1 the Institution may buy on clear, unambiguous specification and pay cash to give the manufacturer liquidity.

rows.name: Industry practice
rows.detail: Istisna today is the project and construction contract: infrastructure, home-building and manufacturing finance, usually as istisna + parallel istisna.
rows.detail_long: Modern usage: the bank contracts istisna with the customer and a parallel istisna with the builder/manufacturer — the structure SS11 clause 7/1 anticipates.
